mainTopic: How many witnesses a סוטה case needs for the defilement, the warning and the seclusion, and the meaning of קינוי
overview: This amud finishes a ברייתא that learns a rule from דברים: when the Torah says עד without a number, it means two witnesses. So the סוטה verse 'ועד אין בה' means there were not two witnesses, only one, and that one witness is enough to forbid her. The גמרא asks why this rule was needed and works through several possible misreadings of the verse. Next it explains the dispute in the משנה. רבי יהושע needs two witnesses for both the warning (קינוי) and the seclusion (סתירה). רבי אליעזר needs two only for the warning, because seclusion is the start of טומאה. A ברייתא then brings רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's reverse report of רבי אליעזר: the warning works on one witness or the husband's own word, while the seclusion needs two. The חכמים object that this has 'no end,' since a husband could falsely claim he warned her, and רבי יוחנן's comment on this objection is reworded. רב חנינא מסורא rules that today a husband should not warn his wife, since there is no bitter water to clear her. The amud ends with ריש לקיש and אביי giving two meanings of the word קינוי, which reflect whether the warning needs witnesses.

steps.title: Why does the verse add the word 'one'?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא points out that the פסוק 'לא יקום עד באיש' already sounds like one witness, so it asks why the Torah adds the word אחד.
steps.simpleTranslation: From the plain words 'A witness shall not rise up against a man,' don't I already know it means one witness? So why does the verse say 'one'?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks why the Torah bothers to write the word 'one' when the verse already sounds singular. This sets up the next step, which gives the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verb יָקוּם ('shall rise up') is singular, so the verse already seems to be about one witness. When the Torah adds an extra word, the ברייתא assumes it must be teaching something new. The answer comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: from the implication of / from what we can already hear in
'a witness shall not rise up against a man' (דברים 19:15)
what does the verse teach by saying...? (pointing to a word that seems extra)

phrases.english: From the implication of what is stated:
"A witness shall not rise up against a man,"
phrases.notes: דברים 19:15. The real פסוק says עֵד אֶחָד; here the word אֶחָד is left out on purpose to make the point.

phrases.english: do I not know that it means one?
phrases.notes: The verb יָקוּם is singular, so you would already hear 'one witness' without the extra word.

phrases.english: What does the verse teach by saying "one"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא from the earlier part of the daf, which set out to prove that עד in the סוטה verse means two witnesses.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the Torah adds the word אחד to a verse that already sounds singular.

steps.title: The general rule: 'witness' means two unless the Torah says 'one'
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא answers that the extra word sets up a בנין אב: wherever the Torah says עד on its own, it means two witnesses, unless it says אחד.
steps.simpleTranslation: This verse set up a general rule: everywhere the Torah says 'witness,' it means two, unless the verse spells out 'one.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its own question. The extra word 'one' teaches a rule for the whole Torah: a plain עד means two witnesses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah only needed to write אחד here because a plain עד would otherwise mean two. So this verse becomes a model, a בנין אב, for every other verse. Wherever the Torah writes עד with no number, we read it as a pair of witnesses.

keyTerms.meaning: set up a model rule (בִּנְיַן אָב) that applies to other places in the Torah
witness; according to this rule, a plain עֵד means two witnesses
until it spells out / specifies

steps.whyThisMatters: This rule is the key to reading the סוטה verse 'ועד אין בה' in the next step.

phrases.english: This established a general rule:
every place where "witness" is stated,
there are two here,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 1.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word אחד sets up a rule: a plain עד in the Torah means two witnesses unless the verse says one.

steps.title: Applying the rule to the סוטה: not two witnesses, only one, and she is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא applies the rule to the סוטה verse: 'ועד אין בה' means there are not two witnesses, only one. Since 'she was not seized,' she is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the Torah said 'there is no witness against her,' meaning there are not two witnesses against her, only one. And 'she was not seized,' so she is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא brings the general rule back to the סוטה. A single witness who saw her act willingly is enough to make her forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because a plain עד means two, 'ועד אין בה' means 'there are not two witnesses,' which leaves room for one. The words 'והיא לא נתפשה' tell us she acted willingly, not by force. With that one witness, she becomes אסורה.

keyTerms.meaning: the Merciful One, a name for ה׳ when quoting the Torah
there are not two (witnesses) against her
'and she was not seized,' meaning she was not forced (במדבר 5:13)
forbidden (to her husband)

steps.whatToRemember: In the סוטה verse, עד means two, so 'ועד אין בה' means only one witness is there, and that one witness is enough to forbid her.

phrases.english: And the Merciful One said:
phrases.notes: He is pointing to the words 'וְעֵד אֵין בָּהּ' in במדבר 5:13, 'there is no witness against her.'

phrases.english: there are not two against her
but only one,

steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: One witness who testifies that a סוטה willingly sinned makes her forbidden, because the verse rules out only two witnesses.

steps.title: Why was the rule needed? With no witness at all, how could she be forbidden?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: the ברייתא makes it sound like, without the rule, we would read the סוטה verse as 'not even one witness.' But then nothing would forbid her, so the reading is obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: But this suggests the only reason is that it is written 'One witness shall not rise up against a man.' Otherwise I would have said the 'witness' in the סוטה verse means one. But if there isn't even one witness, then how does she become forbidden?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions why the ברייתא needed the rule from דברים at all. It seems obvious that the סוטה verse must leave room for one witness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without the rule, 'ועד אין בה' would mean 'there is not even one witness.' Then there would be no testimony at all, and there would be nothing to forbid her. So reading 'one witness is there' seems obvious without any outside source.

keyTerms.meaning: the reason is that it is written...
but if not for this

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for the ברייתא's derivation in steps 1-3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's need for the verse in דברים to explain the סוטה verse.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Reading 'no witness at all' leaves nothing to forbid her, so the verse must mean there is one witness, even without the general rule.

steps.title: Without the rule, we might think one witness is not believed about her
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the rule was needed. Otherwise we might read 'ועד אין בה' as 'a witness is not believed about her,' meaning one witness's testimony would not count.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was needed. You might have thought: 'there is no witness against her' means no single witness is believed about her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the ברייתא needed the rule. Without it, there was another way to misread the סוטה verse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without the rule, we might not read the verse as 'no witness at all.' We might read it as 'a witness has no standing for her,' so one witness would not be believed. The rule from דברים shows that the verse only rules out two witnesses, so one witness is believed.

keyTerms.meaning: it was necessary
it might have entered your mind to say
no witness is believed about her

steps.confusionAlert: The mistaken reading here is different from the one in the question. It is not 'there was no witness at all.' It is 'a single witness is not trusted in her case.' The rule from דברים is what rules out this second reading.
steps.whatToRemember: The rule 'עד means two' is needed so that we do not read the סוטה verse as saying a single witness is not believed about her.

phrases.english: It was necessary,
it might have entered your mind to say:
"there is no witness against her"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that without the rule, there was a different possible misreading.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'ועד אין בה' could mean a single witness is not believed in the case of a סוטה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because a plain עד means two, the verse only rules out two witnesses, and one witness is believed to forbid her.

steps.title: If two witnesses are needed, the verse would be unnecessary
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the reading from Step 5. If 'ועד אין בה' meant 'one witness is not believed, you need two,' the Torah would not need to say it. We already know from the גזירה שוה of 'דבר' 'דבר' that every testimony needs two witnesses.
steps.simpleTranslation: One witness is not believed about her?! Then what does the verse require, two witnesses? Then the verse could have said nothing, because we learn 'matter' 'matter' from money cases. I would already know it, just like all other testimony in the Torah!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the explanation it just gave in Step 5. If the verse only meant 'one witness is not enough,' it would be teaching something we already know.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 said the reading 'a witness is not believed about her' was a real possibility. The גמרא now asks what that reading would add. The need for two witnesses already comes from the גזירה שוה linking 'דבר' in עריות to 'דבר' in ממון. So reading the verse that way makes it useless.

keyTerms.meaning: Let the verse be silent about it. The Torah would not need to write this.
A גזירה שוה built on the shared word 'דבר' (matter)
Money cases, where the Torah says two witnesses are needed
All the kinds of testimony in the Torah

phrases.english: He is not believed about her?!
But then what does it require —
until there are two?
Then let the verse be silent about it.
Since it is learned from 'matter' and 'matter' in money cases.
phrases.notes: 'דבר' appears in דברים 24:1 (about a wife) and in דברים 19:15 (two witnesses for a 'matter').

phrases.english: And I would already know it,
just as with all testimony in the Torah!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין נֶאֱמָן בָּהּ?! וְאֶלָּא מַאי בָּעֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the possible reading suggested in Step 5's תירוץ.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading 'ועד אין בה' as 'one witness is not believed about her'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That reading only teaches that two witnesses are needed, and the גזירה שוה of דבר דבר already teaches that. So the verse would add nothing.

steps.title: A סוטה might have been believed with one witness
steps.stepSummary: The verse was needed. Without it we might think a סוטה is different. The husband's warning and her seclusion already make her suspect, so one witness might have been enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was needed. You might have thought a סוטה is different, because there are already grounds for suspicion: he warned her and she secluded herself. So let one witness be believed about her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the reading from Step 5. It shows that even with the גזירה שוה, the verse still teaches something new about a סוטה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The general rule says two witnesses are needed. But a סוטה case already has evidence pointing toward guilt: the קינוי (warning) and the סתירה (seclusion). So we might have thought one witness is enough to finish the picture. The verse would be telling us that even here, one witness is not believed.

keyTerms.meaning: It was needed. The verse is not extra.
You might have thought (the possible mistaken idea)
Literally 'legs to the matter.' There is already a basis for suspicion.
He warned her, and she secluded herself with that man

phrases.english: It was needed,
because it would enter your mind to say:
A סוטה is different,
since there are 'legs to the matter,'
phrases.notes: The case is already standing on some evidence, so it isn't a story coming out of nowhere.

phrases.english: for he warned her and she secluded herself —
so let one witness be believed about her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 6 by showing that the verse teaches something new for a סוטה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the verse is needed because of a special feature of the case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Because the warning and the seclusion already point to guilt, one witness might be enough for a סוטה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Under this possible reading, the verse would not be extra: it would teach that even for a סוטה, one witness is not believed. The final reading, in step 9, is the opposite: one witness is believed.

steps.title: The verse's own words show she is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא raises a new problem with the reading 'one witness is not believed, so she stays permitted.' The same verse says 'and she was not seized,' which shows it is talking about a woman who becomes forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: But can you really say that one witness is not believed about her and she stays permitted? The verse says 'and she was not seized,' which shows that she is forbidden!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second, stronger objection to the reading from Step 5. It uses the next words of the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'She was not seized' means she was not forced, so she acted willingly. A woman who acted willingly is forbidden to her husband. So the verse is describing a case where she becomes אסורה, and a reading where one witness leaves her permitted does not fit the verse.

keyTerms.meaning: But can you really say? This introduces a strong objection.
She is permitted (to her husband)
By inference. It follows from this.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two objections. Step 6 said the reading makes the verse unnecessary. This step says the reading goes against the verse's own words. The next step answers this objection.

phrases.english: But can you really say
that he is not believed about her and she is permitted?
But from the fact that it is written
'and she was not seized'
phrases.notes: במדבר 5:13. These are the same words the ברייתא used back in Step 3.

phrases.english: it follows that she is forbidden!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי מָצֵית אָמְרַתְּ דְּאֵין נֶאֱמָן בָּהּ וְשַׁרְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a second objection to Step 5's possible reading. It uses the same verse that Step 3 relied on.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that one witness is not believed, so the סוטה stays permitted
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'והיא לא נתפשה' shows she acted willingly, which makes her forbidden. So the verse cannot be describing a case where she stays permitted.

steps.title: The rule was still needed, because the reading could survive the phrase 'she was not seized'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers Step 8. One could still read the verse as 'one witness is not believed, you need two.' Under that reading, even with two witnesses she is forbidden only if she was not forced. So 'והיא לא נתפשה' fits this reading too, and the ברייתא's rule that 'עד' means two is still needed to reject it.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was necessary. You might have thought: one witness is not believed about her until there are two. And even with two, she is forbidden only if 'she was not seized.' So the rule teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the ברייתא against Step 8. The phrase 'she was not seized' does not disprove the wrong reading, so the rule that 'עד' means two is still needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 8 said 'והיא לא נתפשה' shows the verse is about a woman who becomes forbidden, so 'one witness is not believed' cannot be right. The answer is that this reading also has a case where she becomes forbidden: two witnesses saw her, and she was not forced. So the wrong reading is still possible. The ברייתא's rule is needed to fix 'ועד אין בה' as 'there were not two witnesses, but one was there and is believed.'

keyTerms.meaning: It was necessary (the teaching is not extra)

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that the challenged reading can still explain the phrase in the verse, so the rule is still needed.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One witness is not believed. With two witnesses she is forbidden, but only if she was not forced.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'עד' means two, so 'ועד אין בה' means no two witnesses. A single witness is believed.

steps.title: What is the source for רבי יהושע's view?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי יהושע from the משנה: the husband warns her based on two witnesses (and makes her drink based on two). It asks what his source is.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע says: he warns her based on two witnesses, and so on. What is רבי יהושע's reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic in the משנה. It quotes רבי יהושע and asks for his source. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי יהושע needs two witnesses for the warning (קינוי) and for the seclusion (סתירה). רבי אליעזר needs two only for the warning. Now the גמרא wants to know which verse supports רבי יהושע.

keyTerms.meaning: Warns her (the husband's formal warning not to be alone with a certain man)
Based on two witnesses
What is the reason / source?

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר: מְקַנֵּא לָהּ עַל פִּי שְׁנַיִם וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua says: He warns her based on two witnesses, etc.
phrases.notes: 'Etc.' stands for the rest of his words in the משנה: he also makes her drink only based on two witnesses.

phrases.english: What is the reason of Rabbi Yehoshua?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new section, moving from the ברייתא to the משנה's dispute.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which verse is the source for רבי יהושע's need for two witnesses for both warning and seclusion?

steps.title: רבי יהושע learns from 'בה': not for warning, not for seclusion
steps.stepSummary: The word 'בה' ('about her') limits the one-witness rule to the defilement itself. It excludes the warning and also the seclusion. Both of those need two witnesses.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says 'בה,' about it. About it, and not about the warning. 'בה,' and not about the seclusion.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רבי יהושע's source. The word 'בה' means one witness is enough only for the defilement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We learned that one witness is believed about the defilement ('ועד אין בה'). רבי יהושע reads 'בה' as 'in this matter only.' So the warning and the seclusion fall back to the normal rule of two witnesses.

keyTerms.meaning: About her / in it; read here as a limiting word
The husband's warning
Seclusion; being alone with the man

phrases.english: The verse states: 'about her',
phrases.notes: במדבר 5:13, the words 'ועד אין בה'.

phrases.english: about it, and not about the warning,
'about it', and not about the seclusion.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'בה' limits single-witness belief to the defilement. It excludes both קינוי and סתירה, so both need two witnesses.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר learns from 'בה' only to exclude the warning
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר uses 'בה' only to exclude the warning. So the warning needs two witnesses, but the seclusion can be proven with one.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אליעזר says: 'בה,' and not about the warning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains רבי אליעזר's view. He uses the same word 'בה' but draws only one exclusion from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע agree that 'בה' excludes the warning. They disagree about the seclusion. רבי אליעזר does not exclude it, so like the defilement it needs only one witness.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Eliezer says:
'about it', and not about the warning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the other side of the dispute, using the same word.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'בה' excludes only קינוי. סתירה can be proven with one witness, like טומאה.

steps.title: Why doesn't רבי אליעזר also exclude the seclusion?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי אליעזר: 'בה' could just as well exclude the seclusion, the way רבי יהושע reads it.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say: 'בה,' and not about the seclusion!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבי אליעזר. Why not read 'בה' to exclude the seclusion too?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע showed that 'בה' can exclude both the warning and the seclusion. So רבי אליעזר needs a reason to exclude only one of them.

keyTerms.meaning: But let us say (suggesting a different reading)

phrases.english: But say: 'about it', and not about the seclusion!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי אליעזר's reading in Step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אליעזר's limit of 'בה' to excluding only קינוי.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same word could also exclude סתירה, as רבי יהושע reads it. So why stop at one exclusion?

steps.title: Seclusion is linked to defilement in the verse
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר answers that the verse puts seclusion right next to defilement: 'ונסתרה והיא נטמאה.' That link gives them the same rule. Since one witness is enough for defilement, one witness is enough for seclusion too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Seclusion is compared to defilement, as it is written: 'and she was secluded and she was defiled.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי אליעזר. Seclusion cannot be excluded, because the פסוק ties it to defilement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An היקש (linking two things side by side in a פסוק) means they share the same law. Defilement needs only one witness, so seclusion does too. That is why רבי אליעזר uses 'בה' only to exclude the warning.

keyTerms.meaning: Is compared through a side-by-side link in the verse (היקש)
Defilement; here, the act that forbids her
'And she was secluded and she was defiled' (במדבר 5:13)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהושע: two witnesses for both the warning and the seclusion. רבי אליעזר: two witnesses for the warning, but one is enough for the seclusion, because the פסוק links seclusion to defilement.

phrases.english: Seclusion is linked to defilement,
as it is written: 'and she was secluded and she was defiled.'
phrases.notes: במדבר 5:13.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Brings a competing source (an היקש) that blocks the suggested exclusion.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק links seclusion to defilement, so it shares defilement's one-witness rule.

steps.title: The warning is also linked to defilement in a verse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that קינוי is placed next to טומאה in a פסוק, just as סתירה is, so it should also need only one witness.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the warning is also linked to defilement, since it is written: 'And he warned his wife and she was defiled.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבי אליעזר's answer from step 14. The same kind of verse link exists for the warning too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר said סתירה gets the rule of טומאה (one witness) because the פסוק puts them side by side. But another פסוק puts קינוי right next to טומאה. By the same logic, the warning should also need only עד אחד, and then רבי אליעזר's ruling that the warning needs two witnesses falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: The husband's formal warning to his wife not to be alone with a certain man
Is linked by a verse comparison (a הֶיקֵּשׁ), so the two things share a rule
Defilement, meaning the wife actually sinned and became forbidden
Also, too

phrases.english: The warning is also linked to defilement,
as it is written: 'And he warned his wife, and she was defiled'!
phrases.notes: במדבר 5:14

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns רבי אליעזר's own verse-link argument from step 14 against him.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אליעזר's claim that only סתירה shares the one-witness rule of טומאה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If being next to טומאה in a פסוק gives סתירה the one-witness rule, then קינוי, which is also next to טומאה in a פסוק, should get it too.

steps.title: The word 'בה' must exclude at least one of them
steps.stepSummary: The answer is that the Torah wrote 'בה' to exclude something. So at least one of the two cannot follow the one-witness rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the Merciful One excluded with the word 'about her.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that both items can't share the one-witness rule. The word 'בה' tells us that one of them needs two witnesses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both קינוי and סתירה are linked to טומאה. But 'בה' is a limiting word, so it must take something out of the one-witness rule. That forces us to choose one of the two to exclude. Steps 17-22 work out which one.

keyTerms.meaning: Excluded, limited the rule
The Merciful One, meaning the Torah
'About her', the word in the פסוק that limits the one-witness rule

phrases.english: But the Merciful One excluded with 'about her.'
phrases.notes: He means 'בה' has to take something out of the one-witness rule, so not both can share it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A limiting word overrides one of the two verse links
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both קינוי and סתירה would need only one witness, since both are linked to טומאה.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'בה' excludes one of them, so only one can share the one-witness rule.

steps.title: Why exclude the warning and not the seclusion?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what reason there is to say 'בה' excludes קינוי rather than סתירה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what did you see?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבי אליעזר chose to exclude the warning. It is setting up the next move, where reasons are offered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 16 showed that one of the two must be excluded, but it did not say which. רבי יהושע excludes both, and רבי אליעזר excludes only the warning. The גמרא wants a reason to prefer the warning as the excluded one.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And what did you see?', meaning what reason do you have to choose this way
You saw, meaning you decided
An exclusion, here the thing that 'בה' takes out

phrases.english: And what did you see?
phrases.notes: He means: why say 'בה' takes out the warning, and not the seclusion?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on step 16 by asking which item the exclusion should apply to.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A reason to apply the exclusion of 'בה' to קינוי rather than to סתירה.

steps.title: Seclusion is more like defilement because it forbids her
steps.stepSummary: It makes sense to link סתירה with טומאה, because seclusion forbids the wife to her husband just as defilement does.
steps.simpleTranslation: It stands to reason that seclusion is preferable, since it forbids her like defilement.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a reason why seclusion belongs with defilement. Both of them make the wife forbidden to her husband.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once there was a warning and then a seclusion, the wife is forbidden to her husband until she drinks. Defilement also forbids her. So seclusion acts most like defilement, and it should share defilement's rule of עד אחד. That leaves the warning as the one 'בה' excludes.

keyTerms.meaning: It stands to reason, it makes sense
Seclusion, the wife being alone with the man she was warned about
Preferable, the better choice
It forbids her to her husband

phrases.english: It stands to reason that seclusion is preferable,
since it forbids her, like defilement.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: סתירה is more like טומאה because both forbid the wife, so סתירה keeps the one-witness rule and קינוי is excluded.

steps.title: The warning is the main cause
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא argues the opposite: קינוי is the better match for טומאה, because the warning is the root cause of her becoming forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the contrary, the warning is preferable, since it is the main thing that caused it for her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the reason just given and argues the reverse. The warning is what really causes her to be forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the wife is alone with a man without a warning, she does not become forbidden. So the warning is the real cause. By this logic, the warning should share defilement's rule, and seclusion should be the one 'בה' excludes.

keyTerms.meaning: On the contrary
The main thing, the root
Caused

phrases.english: On the contrary: the warning is preferable,
since it is the main thing that caused it for her.
phrases.notes: He means the warning is what makes her forbidden in the first place.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reasoning of step 18 by flipping it.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that סתירה is the better match for טומאה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It ignores that קינוי is the root cause, without which seclusion forbids nothing.

steps.title: Without seclusion, the warning means nothing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: if there is no סתירה, the קינוי by itself accomplishes nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: If not for the seclusion, is there any warning at all?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends seclusion against the 'main cause' argument. A warning alone, with no seclusion, does nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 19 called the warning the main cause. But a warning only matters once the wife actually goes into seclusion. So the warning cannot be called the main cause.

keyTerms.meaning: If not for, without
Is there? Here it means: does it amount to anything?
There is

phrases.aramaic: אִי לָאו סְתִירָה, קִינּוּי מִי אִיכָּא?
phrases.english: If not for seclusion, is there a warning?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי לָאו סְתִירָה קִינּוּי מִי אִיכָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the 'main cause' argument of step 19.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that קינוי is the main cause
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The warning has no effect without the seclusion, so it is not the cause on its own.

steps.title: Without the warning, seclusion is useless too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers back: if there is no קינוי, the סתירה also accomplishes nothing. Each needs the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if not for the warning, what does seclusion accomplish?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the same argument around. Seclusion with no warning also does nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 20 said the warning means nothing without seclusion. The reverse is true as well. Seclusion without a prior warning does not forbid her. So the 'which one is more important' argument ends in a tie, and the next step breaks it.

keyTerms.meaning: What does it accomplish? What effect does it have?
Was effective, helped
What

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the גמרא has decided here. Steps 20 and 21 cancel each other out. Both the warning and the seclusion are needed for her to be forbidden, so neither one is clearly 'more like' defilement yet.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי לָאו קִינּוּי, סְתִירָה מַאי אַהֲנִי?
phrases.english: And if not for the warning, what does seclusion accomplish?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי לָאו קִינּוּי סְתִירָה מַאי אַהֲנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirrors step 20 to cancel out its argument.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The argument of step 20 that seclusion is what matters
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Seclusion is just as useless without the warning, so the argument proves nothing.

steps.title: Seclusion is the better match for defilement
steps.stepSummary: Even though קינוי and סתירה each need the other, סתירה is the better comparison to טומאה, because seclusion is the first stage of defilement.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even so, seclusion is the better choice, because it is the beginning of defilement.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ends the back-and-forth. It decides that סתירה is the one compared to טומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 20-21 showed that neither קינוי nor סתירה works without the other, so that argument was a tie. The tie-breaker is that seclusion is the actual start of the suspected sin. So, just as one witness is enough for טומאה, one witness is enough for סתירה.

keyTerms.meaning: Even so
Is better / preferable
The beginning, the first stage

steps.whatToRemember: According to our משנה (רבי אליעזר), the husband warns her before two witnesses, but one witness to the seclusion is enough to make her drink, because סתירה is the start of טומאה.

phrases.english: Even so, seclusion is preferable,
phrases.notes: He means it is the better thing to compare to defilement.

phrases.english: since it is the beginning of defilement.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Breaks the tie from steps 20-21 in favor of סתירה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: סתירה is compared to טומאה, so one witness suffices for seclusion.

steps.title: A different report of רבי אליעזר's view
steps.stepSummary: The משנה does not follow a ברייתא where רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה quotes רבי אליעזר the opposite way: warning by one witness or by the husband himself, drinking only by two witnesses.
steps.simpleTranslation: Our משנה is not like this תנא. It was taught: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says in the name of רבי אליעזר: one who warns his wife may warn her based on one witness or based on himself, and he makes her drink based on two witnesses.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא showing that another תנא reported רבי אליעזר's opinion in reverse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In our משנה, קינוי needs two witnesses and סתירה needs one. In this ברייתא it is flipped: קינוי needs only one witness, or even just the husband's own word. Making her drink, which depends on proving the סתירה, needs two witnesses.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
Not like this תנא
Based on himself, the husband's own word
Gives her the bitter water to drink

steps.confusionAlert: Both opinions are reports of רבי אליעזר. The dispute is about what רבי אליעזר actually held, and the two reports reverse which stage needs two witnesses.

phrases.english: Our משנה is not in line with this תנא.

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר
phrases.english: As it was taught: רבי יוסי son of רבי יהודה says
in the name of רבי אליעזר:
One who warns his wife,
warns based on one witness
or based on himself,
phrases.notes: The husband can warn her even with no witness at all.

phrases.english: and gives her to drink based on two.
phrases.notes: Two witnesses who saw the seclusion.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After settling the משנה's logic, the גמרא shows another version of רבי אליעזר that disagrees.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Per רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's report: קינוי by one witness or by the husband; drinking only with two witnesses to the seclusion.

steps.title: The Sages object: there would be no end to it
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים respond that according to רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's version, the matter would have no limit.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים replied: according to the words of רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, there is no end to the matter.
steps.whatsHappening: Still inside the ברייתא, the חכמים raise an objection to the view that the warning needs no witnesses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The objection targets the idea that a husband can warn his wife based on one witness or his own word. The text here only says the problem is endless; step 32 explains what that means.

keyTerms.meaning: The חכמים responded
There is no end to the matter

phrases.english: The Sages responded:
According to the words of רבי יוסי son of רבי יהודה,
there is no end to the matter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The חכמים in the ברייתא challenge the view just quoted.
steps.kashyaTarget: Allowing קינוי on one witness or the husband's own word.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Such a lenient rule leads to an endless, unlimited situation.

steps.title: What is רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's source?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reasoning behind רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why he holds that the seclusion needs two witnesses. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה derived from the verse that one witness is enough for סתירה. Now the גמרא wants to know how the other view reads the same verse to reach the opposite result.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?

phrases.aramaic: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה?
phrases.english: What is the reason of רבי יוסי son of רבי יהודה?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the view brought in step 23.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural basis for requiring two witnesses for סתירה.

steps.title: The word ״בָּהּ″ excludes seclusion
steps.stepSummary: He reads ״בָּהּ״ as limiting the one-witness rule to טומאה itself and not to סתירה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says ״בָּהּ״, about it, meaning about the defilement, and not about seclusion.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: he uses the same word ״בָּהּ״ but reads it as excluding סתירה from the one-witness rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One witness works ״בָּהּ״, about the defilement itself. For him, the word comes to exclude seclusion, so seclusion needs the normal two witnesses. This is the reverse of the conclusion in step 22.

keyTerms.meaning: About it (the defilement)

phrases.english: The verse says "about it":
phrases.notes: From ״וְעֵד אֵין בָּהּ״, במדבר 5:13.

phrases.english: about it, and not about seclusion.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 25.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ״בָּהּ״ limits the one-witness rule to טומאה and excludes סתירה.

steps.title: Why not exclude the warning instead?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: maybe ״בָּהּ״ should exclude קינוי, so the warning would also need two witnesses.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say: about it, and not about the warning?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה doesn't also read ״בָּהּ״ as excluding קינוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If ״בָּהּ״ means only defilement gets the one-witness rule, the warning should be excluded too. Yet he allows a warning on one witness, so his reading seems inconsistent.

keyTerms.meaning: But let us say
The husband's warning

phrases.english: But say: "about it," and not about the warning?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how far the exclusion in step 26 reaches.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's ruling that קינוי works on one witness.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If ״בָּהּ״ excludes everything except טומאה, it should exclude קינוי as well.

steps.title: Warning and defilement are linked in the verse
steps.stepSummary: קינוי is placed right next to טומאה in the verse, so it shares the one-witness rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: The warning is linked to defilement, as it is written: "And he warned his wife, and she was defiled."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the verse itself joins the warning to defilement, so ״בָּהּ״ cannot exclude it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the פסוק mentions קינוי and טומאה together, they are compared in law (a היקש). So whatever works for טומאה, like one witness, also works for קינוי. Only סתירה is left for ״בָּהּ״ to exclude.

keyTerms.meaning: Is linked by a היקש (placed side by side in the verse)
As it is written

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה: קינוי is tied to טומאה by the verse, so it needs only one witness; ״בָּהּ″ excludes סתירה, which needs two.

phrases.english: The warning is juxtaposed to defilement,
as it is written: "And he warned his wife,
and she was defiled."
phrases.notes: במדבר 5:14

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 27.
steps.terutzMaskana: קינוי is linked to טומאה by the verse, so only סתירה is excluded.

steps.title: Seclusion is also placed next to defilement in the verse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: if קינוי shares the one-witness rule because it sits next to טומאה, then סתירה should too, because the פסוק links סתירה with טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But seclusion is also linked to defilement, since the verse says: 'And she was secluded and she was defiled'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from the last step. If being next to טומאה in the פסוק gives קינוי the one-witness rule, then סתירה should get it too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 28, the גמרא said קינוי gets the one-witness rule because the פסוק puts it right next to טומאה. But the words 'ונסתרה והיא נטמאה' put סתירה right next to טומאה as well. So by the same logic, סתירה should also be proven with one witness. That would contradict רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, who requires two witnesses for סתירה.

keyTerms.meaning: Seclusion: the wife being alone with the man her husband warned her about
Is compared or linked, because the פסוק places the two things together
Here: the wife becoming forbidden through adultery
Also, too

phrases.english: Seclusion is also linked to defilement,
as it is written: "And she was secluded and she was defiled"?!
phrases.notes: במדבר 5:13

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same reasoning as step 28's answer and turns it against סתירה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that only קינוי, and not סתירה, shares the one-witness rule of טומאה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If being placed next to טומאה is enough for קינוי, then סתירה, which is also placed next to טומאה, should share the rule too.

steps.title: The link teaches the length of seclusion
steps.stepSummary: The link between סתירה and טומאה in the פסוק teaches how long the seclusion must be: enough time for טומאה. It does not teach the witness rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: That verse comes to teach how long seclusion has to be: enough time for defilement to happen.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The link between סתירה and טומאה is used to teach something else, so it can't also teach the witness rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'ונסתרה והיא נטמאה' teach that seclusion only counts if it lasts long enough for טומאה to happen. Since that link is already used for the length of time, it is not used to give סתירה the one-witness rule. So סתירה still needs two witnesses, while קינוי gets the one-witness rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Measure or amount, here the length of time
Enough time for defilement (adultery) to happen
That is what it comes to teach

steps.whyThisMatters: This gives the rule that seclusion only counts when it lasts long enough for adultery to happen.

phrases.english: That verse is about how much is the measure of seclusion:
enough time for defilement. That is what it comes to teach.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 29.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redirects the verse to teach a different law
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The link between סתירה and טומאה would give סתירה the one-witness rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: The link only teaches the minimum time of seclusion, so סתירה still needs two witnesses.

steps.title: What does 'no end to the matter' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא repeats the חכמים's reply to רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה and asks what 'there is no end to the matter' means.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis responded: according to רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, there is no end to the matter. What does that mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the ברייתא and repeats the חכמים's reply. It is setting up a question: what exactly is the 'no end' problem?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 24 already quoted these words. Now the גמרא repeats them to explain them. The phrase is unclear, so the גמרא asks what 'endless' problem the חכמים had in mind.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages responded
There is no end to the matter: the rule opens the door to endless problems
What is it? What does it mean?

phrases.english: The Rabbis responded:
According to the words of Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda,
phrases.notes: He means רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's version of רבי אליעזר's view: one witness for the warning, two for the seclusion.

phrases.english: there is no end to the matter.
What is it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of the verse and returns to explain the ברייתא from step 24.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the חכמים's objection 'there is no end to the matter'

steps.title: The husband could falsely claim he warned her
steps.stepSummary: The problem is that a husband who never warned his wife could later say 'I warned her,' and his word alone would be enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: Sometimes he did not warn her, and he says 'I warned her.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the 'no end' problem. If the husband himself can establish the warning, he might lie about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's version, קינוי can be established by one witness or by the husband himself. So a husband could hear that his wife was alone with a man and only then claim he had warned her. That would make her forbidden to him until she drinks, even though no real warning happened.

keyTerms.meaning: Sometimes
Warned (gave the קינוי)
"I warned": the husband's claim

phrases.english: That sometimes he did not warn her,
and he says "I warned her."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 31.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The husband could lie and claim he warned her, and since he alone can establish the warning, she becomes forbidden.

steps.title: The same problem exists in our משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: in our משנה's version, the husband's word can establish the seclusion, so he could just as easily lie about that.
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to our משנה, is there an end to the matter? Sometimes she was not secluded, and he says 'she was secluded'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the explanation. Our משנה's version has the same problem, so why did the חכמים complain only about רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's version?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In our משנה, רבי אליעזר says the wife drinks based on one witness or the husband's own word about סתירה. So a husband could falsely claim she was secluded. The risk of lying exists there too. So it is strange that the חכמים aimed their 'no end' complaint only at רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's version.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה: the version of רבי אליעזר's view in our משנה
There is an end to the matter
Was secluded

phrases.english: But according to our משנה, is there an end to the matter?
Sometimes she was not secluded,
and he says "she was secluded"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the explanation of step 32 by showing the same problem exists in the משנה's version.
steps.kashyaTarget: Why the חכמים complained only about רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's version
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the משנה's version the husband's word establishes seclusion, so he could lie there too. The 'no end' problem is not unique to רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's version.

steps.title: Even in this version there is no end
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains that the חכמים meant 'even according to רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה there is no end,' and certainly according to our משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יצחק בר יוסף said in the name of רבי יוחנן: even according to רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, there is no end to the matter.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers by reading the חכמים's words with the word 'even.' Their complaint applies to both versions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים were not saying that only רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's version has the problem. They meant: even in his version, where סתירה needs two witnesses, the husband can still lie about the warning. All the more so in our משנה's version, where he can also lie about the seclusion.

keyTerms.meaning: Even

steps.whatToRemember: This first version of רבי יוחנן's statement is challenged in the next step and reworded in step 36, so do not treat it as the final word.
steps.confusionAlert: This is only the first version of רבי יוחנן's statement. The next step challenges its 'even this, and all the more so that' order, and step 36 rewords it.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יִצְחָק בַּר יוֹסֵף אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rav Yitzchak bar Yosef said that Rabbi Yochanan said:

phrases.aramaic: אַף לְדִבְרֵי רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
phrases.english: Even according to the words of Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda,
there is no end to the matter.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַף לְדִבְרֵי רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אֵין לַדָּבָר סוֹף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 33 by rereading the חכמים's words.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The חכמים meant only רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's version has the 'no end' problem.
steps.terutzMaskana: The חכמים meant 'even' his version has the problem, and certainly our משנה's version.

steps.title: Challenging the order of רבי יוחנן's statement
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא argues that רבי יוחנן's 'even רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, and certainly our משנה' is backwards, because our משנה's version has a solid basis and רבי יוסי's version does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Even according to רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, and certainly according to our משנה'? Just the opposite! In our משנה there is a solid basis, while there, in רבי יוסי's version, there is no solid basis!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the way רבי יוחנן worded the answer in the last step. It says his 'even this, and all the more so that' order is the wrong way around.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'even X, and certainly Y' means the problem is harder to see in X and easier to see in Y. But in our משנה's version, witnesses saw the warning, so there is a real basis for suspicion and trusting the husband about the seclusion is understandable. In רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's version, the warning itself rests only on the husband's word, so there is no firm basis at all. That is where the 'no end' worry is strongest.

keyTerms.meaning: On the contrary; just the opposite
A solid basis or foundation (here, a warning proven by witnesses)
And it is not even necessary to say; all the more so
Our משנה (the version in our משנה)

phrases.aramaic: אַף לְדִבְרֵי רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה,
phrases.english: Even according to the words of רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה,
and certainly according to our משנה?
On the contrary: according to our משנה there is a solid basis,
phrases.notes: The 'basis' is the warning, which witnesses saw.

phrases.english: there, there is no solid basis!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the logic of רבי יוחנן's answer in step 34.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's 'even רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, and certainly our משנה' wording.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The 'no end' concern is stronger where there is no firm basis (רבי יוסי's version), so it cannot be 'all the more so' for our משנה, which has a firm basis.

steps.title: Rewording רבי יוחנן's statement
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says רבי יוחנן's statement must have been the other way around: the 'no end' objection applies to רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's version, and even to our משנה's version.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, if it was said, this is how it was said: רב יצחק בר יוסף said in the name of רבי יוחנן: According to the words of רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה there is no end to the matter, and even according to our משנה there is no end to the matter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the problem by giving a new version of what רבי יוחנן said. Now the order fits the logic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the new version, רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's version is the obvious case, since it has no firm basis. The new point is that the חכמים's objection reaches even our משנה's version, where the warning has witnesses but the husband is trusted about the seclusion. So the 'even' now goes on the harder case, as it should.

keyTerms.meaning: If it was said, this is how it was said (a formula for rewording a statement)
There is no end to the matter (the husband could invent claims)

phrases.english: Rather, if it was stated, it was stated like this:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יִצְחָק בַּר יוֹסֵף אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: רב יצחק בר יוסף said that רבי יוחנן said:
According to the words of רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה,
even according to our משנה there is no end to the matter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 35 by changing the wording of רבי יוחנן's statement.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rewording of the earlier statement (changing the order of the 'even' claim).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוחנן said the objection applies 'even' to רבי יוסי's version and 'certainly' to our משנה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The objection clearly applies to רבי יוסי's version, and the new point is that it applies even to our משנה's version.
steps.whatToRemember: The חכמים's worry, 'there is no end to the matter,' clearly hits רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's version, and per רבי יוחנן it reaches even our משנה's version.

steps.title: Nowadays a man should not warn his wife
steps.stepSummary: רב חנינא מסורא rules that today a husband should not warn his wife, because she might become forbidden to him forever, with no bitter water to clear her.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חנינא מסורא said: Nowadays a man should not tell his wife, 'Do not be alone with so-and-so.' Perhaps the הלכה follows רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, who says a warning works on the husband's own word. Then she might go and be alone with that man, and today there is no סוטה water to test her, so he would make her forbidden to himself forever.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a practical ruling. Since we are not sure the halacha is unlike רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, a husband today should avoid giving a warning at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a warning followed by seclusion leads to the bitter water test, which can make the wife permitted again. Today there is no such test, so if she secludes herself she stays forbidden with no way out. Since even a private warning might count (by רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה), the safe path is not to warn.

keyTerms.meaning: Nowadays, in our times
Do not seclude yourself (the wording of the warning)
A warning that counts based on the husband's own word
The bitter water used to test a סוטה
A permanent prohibition

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a practical guideline for today: since the bitter water no longer exists, a warning could create a prohibition with no remedy.

phrases.english: רב חנינא from Sura said:

phrases.aramaic: לָא לֵימָא אִינִישׁ לְאִיתְּתֵיהּ בַּזְּמַן הַזֶּה
phrases.english: A man should not say to his wife nowadays
'Do not seclude yourself with so-and-so,'

phrases.aramaic: דִּילְמָא קַיְימָא לַן כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה,
phrases.english: since perhaps we hold like רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה,
who says a warning works on his own word,
and she then secludes herself,
and nowadays there is no סוטה water to test her,
and he forbids her to himself with a permanent prohibition.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חֲנִינָא מִסּוּרָא: לָא לֵימָא אִינִישׁ לְאִיתְּתֵיהּ בַּזְּמַן הַזֶּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a practical lesson from the debate over רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's view.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Nowadays a husband should not warn his wife, because the warning might take effect and, with no bitter water, she could become permanently forbidden to him.

steps.title: ריש לקיש explains the word קינוי
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש says the word קינוי means something that creates bad feeling between the woman and other people.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: What does the word 'קינוי' mean? Something that creates jealousy and bad feeling between her and others.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching begins. ריש לקיש explains why the warning is called קינוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He links קינוי to the word קנאה, jealousy or anger. The warning causes friction, because the wife starts avoiding certain men and they resent it.

keyTerms.meaning: The husband's warning to his wife
Jealousy, anger, bad feeling
The wording or meaning of a term

phrases.english: ריש לקיש said: What is the meaning of the term 'warning'?

phrases.aramaic: דָּבָר הַמֵּטִיל קִנְאָה בֵּינָהּ לְבֵין אֲחֵרִים.
phrases.english: A matter that puts bad feeling between her and others.
phrases.notes: ריש לקיש hears the word קנאה, anger or jealousy, inside the word קינוי.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: מָה לְשׁוֹן קִינּוּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: the meaning of the word קינוי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: קינוי means a matter that causes bad feeling between the wife and others.

steps.title: So ריש לקיש holds a warning works on the husband's word
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא infers that ריש לקיש holds the warning can be on the husband's own word, so people don't know about it and resent the woman for avoiding them.
steps.simpleTranslation: It seems he holds that a warning works on the husband's own word. So nobody else knows he warned her, and they say, 'What is going on here, that she keeps away from us?' Then they come to feel anger toward her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a conclusion from ריש לקיש's explanation: his reason only makes sense if the warning can be given privately.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If witnesses had to see the warning, people would know why she avoids them and would not be upset. The bad feeling only happens because the warning was private and others don't know about it. So ריש לקיש must agree with רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה that a warning works on the husband's own word.

keyTerms.meaning: It appears, so we see (introduces an inference)
He holds, he is of the opinion
She keeps away, separates herself

steps.whatToRemember: ריש לקיש's explanation of קינוי shows that he holds a warning can work on the husband's own word, like רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה.

phrases.aramaic: אַלְמָא קָסָבַר קִינּוּי עַל פִּי עַצְמוֹ,
phrases.english: Apparently he holds a warning works on his own word,

phrases.aramaic: וְכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא יָדְעִי דְּקַנִּי לַהּ,
phrases.english: and everyone else does not know that he warned her,
and they say: What is this before us, that she keeps away?
and they come to act with anger toward her.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַלְמָא קָסָבַר קִינּוּי עַל פִּי עַצְמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference about ריש לקיש's legal view from his explanation of the word in step 38.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: ריש לקיש holds that a warning works on the husband's own word, because the bad feeling only makes sense if others don't know about the warning.

steps.title: A second meaning of the word קינוי: bad feeling between husband and wife
steps.stepSummary: רב יימר בר רבי שלמיא, quoting אביי, explains that קינוי means something that brings bad feeling between the husband and his wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב יימר בר רבי שלמיא said in the name of אביי: קינוי means something that puts bad feeling between him and her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second explanation of the word קינוי, different from the one ריש לקיש gave in step 38.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש said the bad feeling is between the woman and other people. Here אביי says the bad feeling is between the husband and the wife themselves. The next step will show why this difference matters.

keyTerms.meaning: Jealousy, bad feeling or anger between people
Something that puts or casts (bad feeling)
Between him and her: between the husband and the wife
In the name of (someone)

phrases.english: And Rav Yeimar bar Rabbi Shelemya
said in the name of Abaye:
a matter that puts bad feeling
phrases.notes: He is explaining the word קינוי from the משנה, just as ריש לקיש did a moment ago.

phrases.english: between him and her.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב יֵימַר בַּר רַבִּי שֶׁלֶמְיָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּאַבָּיֵי אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second definition of קינוי, parallel to and different from ריש לקיש's definition in step 38.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: קינוי means something that creates bad feeling between the husband and the wife.

steps.title: What אביי's explanation shows: the warning needs two witnesses
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא infers that אביי holds a warning must be given before two witnesses. Since everyone knows about it, the bad feeling is only between the husband and his wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: It seems he holds that a warning is given before two witnesses. Everyone knows the husband warned her, so people do not resent her. It is the husband himself who ends up with bad feeling toward her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what lies behind אביי's definition: in his view, the warning is given in front of two witnesses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the warning is public through two witnesses, other people understand why the woman stays away from a certain man, so they are not upset with her. The only tension left is between the husband and wife. This is the opposite of step 39, where ריש לקיש held the warning can be on the husband's word alone, so people did not know about it and resented her.

keyTerms.meaning: Apparently; it follows that
He holds (this opinion)
Based on two witnesses
Everyone; the whole world
With her

steps.whatToRemember: The two definitions of קינוי reflect a deeper disagreement. ריש לקיש holds the warning can be on the husband's own word, so others resent her. אביי holds it needs two witnesses, so everyone knows, and the tension is between husband and wife.

phrases.english: Apparently he holds
a warning is based on two witnesses,
and everyone knows that he warned her,
and it is he who comes
to have bad feeling with her.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַלְמָא קָסָבַר קִינּוּי עַל פִּי שְׁנַיִם עֵדִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws out the legal view hidden inside אביי's definition from step 40, mirroring the inference made about ריש לקיש in step 39.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: אביי holds that the warning must be given before two witnesses. Because it is public, the bad feeling is between husband and wife, not between the woman and others.
